page.title: Best 80 Amp EV Charger (2026): Grizzl-E vs Autel vs GM and Ford
page.desc: 80 A (19.2 kW) home EV chargers compared: the Grizzl-E Ultimate 80A for most buyers, the Autel MaxiCharger 80A for Ethernet and two-charger homes, and which cars can use 80 A.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best 80 amp EV charger for most buyers is the Grizzl-E Ultimate 80A. It gives 80 A (19.2 kW), a 25 ft cable and Wi-Fi for $599.99 at the maker, seen 2026-11-17. Choose the Autel MaxiCharger 80A ({buy:autel-maxicharger-80a-19-2kw}) if your garage needs a wired connection or two EVs must share one circuit. It has Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and an Ethernet port, shares power between two Autel chargers with no extra hardware, and has a 5-year warranty.

Check your car first. An 80 A charger only beats a 48 A charger if the car has a 19.2 kW onboard charger. Examples are the extended-range F-150 Lightning, every 2027 Escalade IQ and the Lucid Air Grand Touring; most other EVs stop at 48 A (11.5 kW). Both chargers need a dedicated 100 A breaker, and your panel may not have room for one.

Home backup with an F-150 Lightning and Ford Home Integration System

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • Paying for 80 A the car can't use. This was the most common theme, raised in 5 of the sources we read. In a Lucid owners thread, an Air Pure owner on an Autel 80A sees about 9 kW. An Air Grand Touring owner on the same charger sees 79 to 80 A.
  • Getting the Autel online. In the same thread, 3 of 4 Autel 80A owners described connection trouble. One said the charger would not start until it was online and used a powerline Ethernet kit. Another gave up on Wi-Fi and ran it offline for about two years with no hardware fault. Autel's store page now lists Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Ethernet. If the garage is far from your router, plan an Ethernet run.
  • The install. Full 80 A needs a dedicated 100 A breaker and heavy wire. Get a load calculation before you buy. Ask the electrician to confirm the charger's terminals take the wire size your run needs.

Which one by need

  • One 19.2 kW EV at the lowest price: Grizzl-E Ultimate 80A, $599.99 at the maker (2026-11-17). It comes with a J1772 or NACS plug and is UL listed and Energy Star certified.
  • Weak garage Wi-Fi, or two EVs on one circuit: Autel MaxiCharger 80A. It has an Ethernet port, shares power between two Autel units, comes with a 5-year warranty and has a NEMA 4X case. It has a J1772 plug only, so NACS cars need an adapter.
  • Home backup from a GM EV: GM Energy PowerShift Charger (19.2 kW). It supports vehicle-to-home on compatible 2026 GM EVs with GM's separate kit.
  • Home backup from an F-150 Lightning: Ford Charge Station Pro (80 A) with Ford's Home Integration System. Ford recommends it for the standard-range truck only if you want home backup.

Not recommended

Don't buy an 80 A charger for a car that tops out at 48 A or less. A 48 A charger on a 60 A breaker charges it just as fast and costs less to wire. If you need a whole-home load limit, the Grizzl-E 80A product page doesn't list one. Autel's whole-home limit (ALM) needs extra hardware that the store page doesn't price.
